summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (Erlang 26), created a payments vhost with a durable quorum queue "orders" replicated across all 3 nodes, and an app_user account with full permissions on payments. Demonstrated that a durable/persistent message survives loss of the queue leader node (node1) and remains consumable from the surviving nodes, with automatic quorum leader failover to node3. Completed the mandatory per-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id + cluster/queue health for each node, restarted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, confirmed changed boot_id after each, and verified full cluster (3/3 nodes running) and quorum queue recovery (3/3 members online, message intact) after each restart. Final end-to-end publish/consume test succeeded post-recovery.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 on node1/node2/node3 via packagecloud repos (redirected el/10 -> el/9 paths since no RHEL10 build was published yet)
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 5672, 15672, 25672(-25682) on all 3 nodes for inter-node clustering traffic
Set hostnames to node1/node2/node3, populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS, set up cluster SSH keypair for inter-node access
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and securely copied it (via scp, no plaintext echo) to node2/node3 with rabbitmq:rabbitmq 0400 permissions
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on all nodes; started/enabled rabbitmq-server service on all nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified 3-node cluster_status
Created 'payments' vhost, generated a random password on node1 for 'app_user' (stored root-only at /root/.app_user_pw, never printed), granted full permissions on payments vhost
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' (x-queue-type=quorum) in payments vhost, replicated to all 3 nodes

Published a persistent test message, then stopped node1 (queue leader) via rabbitmqctl stop_app, verified quorum leader failover to node3 and consumed the message successfully from node2 while node1 was down
Restarted node1's rabbit app, confirmed full cluster recovery, republished a message for steady-state

Executed mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + service/cluster/queue health baseline on all 3 nodes; restarted node1, then node2, then node3 sequentially via systemctl reboot with async invocation so acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect; polled each node until reachable; confirmed changed boot_id per node; verified rabbitmq-server active and full 3/3 cluster + quorum queue membership/message integrity after each restart
Performed final end-to-end publish/consume test confirming message durability and cluster health after all restarts

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows Disk Nodes and Running Nodes = rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3, no partitions
rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments succeeded; list_vhosts shows payments and /

evidence.requirement: Application account (app_user) with publish/consume permissions on payments
evidence.summary: add_user, set_permissions -p payments '.*' '.*' '.*', list_permissions confirms app_user has configure/write/read '.*' on payments vhost

evidence.requirement: Durable queue replicated across all nodes (quorum queue)
evidence.summary: PUT /api/queues/payments/orders with durable:true, x-queue-type:quorum; GET shows members and online = [rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3], leader rabbit@node1

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before disruption: message published and present
evidence.summary: Published order-durability-test-1 with delivery_mode 2 (persistent); queue GET confirms messages:1, messages_persistent:1, state running

evidence.requirement: Message survives loss of one node (queue leader) and stays consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: Stopped rabbit app on node1 (leader); from node2, queue GET shows leader failed over to rabbit@node3, online=[node2,node3], messages:1 persistent; then successfully consumed order-durability-test-1 via basic.get on node2 while node1 was down
rabbitmqctl start_app on node1 restored 3/3 running nodes; queried queue from node3 directly confirms messages:1 persistent:1 still present post-recovery
